rationale:
COMMENT AND TEST ONLY - no behaviour change. Correcting a false invariant this lane itself wrote, and covering a branch that had zero tests.

The doc comment at rewrite_negations_action.go's unansweredTargetRejections call site claims `targets == len(rewritten) + len(rejected)` holds 'for every marker'. Measured on v1.0.1332, the first day the target-accounting fix (council f3046f0c) was live, that is false in BOTH directions. The precise form is:

  targets == len(rewritten) + len(rejected) - count(reason="no_such_sentence"), and ONLY for status='repaired'

(1) UNDER-COUNT, already recorded as bugs_open/305 §27a: five early returns (lines 454, 458, 540, 559, 570) all precede the accounting call at 665, so a repair_unavailable marker accounts for none of its targets by design; its `error` field names which reason fired.

(2) OVER-COUNT, new, and found in production rather than by reasoning: a replacement naming a sentence that is in no target is rejected as `no_such_sentence` - an entry with NO target behind it - so it pushes the sum ABOVE targets. On 2026-08-23 I reasoned my way to this branch, queried the data, found it had NEVER fired in a live window, and recorded it in RUNBOOK §9 as the column that would signal something new rather than the known hole. On 2026-08-24 it fired: exactly 1 marker of 122 post-roll, targets=5 rewritten=4 rejected=2 - the 2 being one no_answer_for_target (the fifth target, correctly recorded) and one no_such_sentence (a sentence the model invented, correctly logged). All five targets accounted for; the sum is six because the model said six things. The ACCOUNTING is right; the sentence describing it was wrong.

Why this matters beyond tidiness: a census written against the loose form flags healthy markers as defects, and the tempting response is to loosen matchTarget until every replacement finds a target - which would splice a rewrite into copy the model was not describing. That is the failure this change defends against.

no_such_sentence had ZERO test coverage (grep -c on the test file: 0).

On the test's design, pre-empting the objection this lane drew on 08-23: it carries NO closing arithmetic assertion, and says so in a comment. The obvious closer computes rewritten + hallucinated - hallucinated == len(targets) from three constants the test itself chose, so it holds whatever the code does - a vacuous assertion that would read as coverage of the census formula and check nothing. What is testable in a unit is the DISCRIMINATION, and that is mutation-proven: dropping the containment check in matchTarget makes the test fail on exactly its load-bearing assertion. The formula itself is verified where it can actually fail - against production markers.

Verified with scripts/verify-head-builds.sh --with, because the working tree does not currently compile: another session's refresh_evidence_base_action.go:769 has `undefined: discovery_checks`. That is not this change, and it is why a first mutation run returned an inconclusive BUILD failure rather than a test failure - worth stating because a build failure and a caught mutation look identical at the exit code.

NOTE ON THIS SUBMISSION'S SHAPE. The change is two files: the corrected comment (quoted in full above and in grounded_in) and the new test. Only the test appears in .plan.edits, because the gate's client-side check correctly refuses a comment-only sketch - 'a fix plan proposes changes, not observations' - and directs such content to .rationale. So the reviewable code here is the test; the comment is the finding it documents. Both land in one commit.

plan.summary: Add the missing test for the no_such_sentence branch (zero prior coverage), pinning that matchTarget REFUSES a sentence present in no target while still matching every real target. Shipped alongside a corrected doc comment stating the reconciliation invariant precisely (see rationale). No behaviour change.

edits.rationale: no_such_sentence had zero coverage. The test pins the discrimination that matters: matchTarget must REFUSE a sentence present in no target, while still matching every real target by its own sentence (so the guard is selective rather than blind). Mutation-proven - dropping the containment check makes it fail on that assertion.

grounded_in: The comment being corrected, verbatim: 'Recorded as a rejection with its own reason rather than silently dropped, so that `targets == len(rewritten) + len(rejected)` holds for every marker'.
Production census 2026-08-24, post-roll (status='repaired', updated_at > 09:40Z): 122 markers, 247 targets, not_reconciling 1, over_counted 1, account_for_none 0.

The single over-counted marker: targets=5, rewritten=4, rejected=2, reasons = 'no_such_sentence, no_answer_for_target' - so all 5 targets are accounted and the excess is exactly the 1 hallucinated replacement.
The demand control for the accounting fix itself, same window: no_answer_for_target fired 43 times, alongside still_rather_than 8, still_negative_reveal 4, still_x_not_y 1, no_such_sentence 1.
Zero prior coverage: grep -c 'no_such_sentence' on rewrite_negations_action_test.go returned 0 before this change.
The five early returns that produce direction (1), by line: 454 (no ai_service), 458 (ai client), 540 (call error), 559 (output ceiling), 570 (unparseable) - all above the accounting call at 665.

RUNBOOK §9 as written on 2026-08-23, which predicted this exact column: 'over_counted is the column that would catch a REGRESSION... Measured 2026-08-23: 0, and no_such_sentence has never fired in a live window - so a non-zero reading there is new information, not the known hole.'
plan.risks:
LOWEST-RISK SHAPE AVAILABLE: one comment block and one test function; no exported symbol, no config key, no schema, no control flow touched. The chassis build in flight is unaffected either way.

The real risk is the OPPOSITE change, and this edit exists to make it fail loudly: if a future session sees a non-zero over_counted and 'fixes' it by loosening matchTarget until every replacement finds a target, rewrites get spliced into copy the model was not describing. That is a silent content defect, and the new test is the tripwire.

TEST-DESIGN RISK, stated rather than hidden: a reviewer may want a closing assertion on the census formula. There deliberately is none, because every term of it is a constant the test chooses, so it would pass regardless of the code - the vacuous shape flagged at this lane on 08-23. The formula is asserted against production data in bugs_open/305 §29 instead.

NOT FIXED HERE: the invariant remains descriptive rather than enforced - nothing in the code computes it. Enforcing it would mean the action asserting its own marker arithmetic at runtime, which is a behaviour change and out of scope for a comment correction.
